title: Local thickness refinement of 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 dual-band mid-IR filter on Daimon-20 substrate
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness perturbations to ±15 nm around the iteration-16 best candidate will improve target score by resolving fine-scale interference conditions without disrupting the established macroscopic topology that already achieves ~0.92 target performance.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: transmission peaks in multilayer stacks arise from constructive interference at specific wavelengths, controlled by optical path lengths (n×d). Small thickness adjustments (~λ/100 scale at mid-IR) can shift phase relationships enough to improve passband transmission while maintaining stopband rejection. The 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternation provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization.
proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 coating layers total)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses, each constrained to ±15 nm around the iteration-16 best candidate values
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band (methane)
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band (carbon dioxide)
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band (suppression)
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band (suppression)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
ZnS and Al2O3 are conventional depositable IR materials
Thickness tolerances of ±15 nm are achievable with modern deposition monitoring
theory_basis: Recalled: High/low index alternation creates photonic stopbands via Bragg reflection
Recalled: Transmission windows can be engineered by breaking periodicity with strategic thickness variations
Recalled: Mid-IR wavelengths (3-5 μm) require layer thicknesses on order of 500-1500 nm for quarter-wave conditions
Recalled: ZnS has higher refractive index (~2.2-2.4 in mid-IR) than Al2O3 (~1.6-1.7), providing sufficient index contrast
Recalled: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in mid-IR and serves as suitable substrate
expected_advantages: Focused local search avoids wasting iterations on topologically inferior regions
±15 nm constraint preserves the macroscopic interference pattern already optimized
Fine tuning may resolve phase mismatches that limit the 0.9202 score
Maintains material pair consistency for fair comparison across control route iterations
known_risks: Uncertain whether ±15 nm window is wide enough to escape local optima - if no improvement occurs, widening to ±30 nm would need to be tested
Recalled ZnS and Al2O3 mid-IR extinction coefficients are approximate; actual absorption may limit achievable transmittance
Uncertain whether 22 layers is optimal vs. fewer layers with different topology - but changing layer count would be a different axis
Daimon-20 substrate refractive index dispersion in mid-IR not precisely recalled; registry data will resolve this
No polarization or angle specification in original request; assuming normal incidence which may not match actual sensor geometry
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 coating layers). Initialize thicknesses at: [909.4, 804.2, 708.0, 683.0, 344.8, 1221.0, 362.2, 576.3, 876.3, 627.6, 371.9, 1154.2, 336.7, 467.5, 850.9, 419.4, 829.2, 1274.1, 929.2, 420.9, 806.8, 881.9] nm (iteration-16 best candidate). Constrain each thickness to ±15 nm around these center values. Optimize for: maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands; minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. Use coherent transfer matrix method. Normal incidence, unpolarized. No metal layers. Total layer count fixed at 22.
revision_reason: Transition from global exploration to focused local search: constrain perturbation amplitudes to ±15 nm centered on the iteration-16 best candidate to resolve fine-scale constructive interference conditions without disrupting the established macroscopic topology.
